findings.desc: CHK-005:happy:1 partial coverage: the intent specifies rollback-fired, no-progress-stop, and human-gate-precision as individually reported counts with known fixture values, but the implementation collapses all three into the safe-stop outcome superset because the bare §7 run-record does not include process-events. The evidence discloses this honestly, but the must-priority intent was not satisfied: the analysis script does not emit separate rollback-fired / no-progress-stop / human-gate-precision counts (only the safe-stop aggregate is reported). The disclosed behavior is a real scope narrowing relative to the CHK-005 context (§4.2: report secondary detectors individually).
findings.resolvedReason: secondaryDetectors reports rollback/human-gate/no-progress individually when terminalStopType/processEvents present (else aggregate+note); selfcheck det2 asserts breakdown; commit 4de4ce33a

findings.desc: CHK-002:happy:2 precision gap: the intent requires Wilson CI bounds to match the textbook Wilson formula to 6+ decimal places against a known-good reference value. The evidence asserts wilson(8,10) with range checks (lo<0.8<hi, lo>0.4, hi<0.99) and approx(p, 0.8, 1e-9), which verifies the formula is not wildly wrong but does not compute the closed-form textbook CI bounds and compare them to 6 decimal places. WHY the intent specifies this: verifies CI computation correctness against a known-good reference, not just plausibility. The actual test is plausibility-level, not formula-precision-level.
findings.resolvedReason: Wilson selfcheck now formula-precise vs closed-form at 9dp; commit 4de4ce33a

findings.desc: dead-code: analyze.mjs:30 imports A2PRIME_BUDGET_FIELDS from run-driver.mjs but it is never referenced anywhere in analyze.mjs; the a2primeBudgetCompliance function accesses budgetPass/tokenInBand/wallInBand directly from record fields without using this constant

dead-code: analyze-selfcheck.mjs:195 uses no-op .replace(/\\s/g, m => m) before the regex test for the glmm.R random-effect syntax — the identity transform changes nothing (every whitespace char replaced with itself), making it dead code; the regex already covers both spaced and compact forms via alternation so the replace is not needed
findings.resolvedReason: removed dead .replace no-op in glmm.R regex test; commit 4de4ce33a

findings.desc: dead-code: analyze.mjs:471 the ternary `res ? applyValidityFilter(recs).kept : []` has an unreachable false branch — analyze() always returns a non-null object so res is always truthy; the empty-array fallback can never execute; the applyValidityFilter call is also a redundant re-filter of already-filtered data (analyze() already applies the filter internally)
findings.resolvedReason: main() computes kept once + reuses for CSV emit (removed unreachable branch + redundant re-filter); commit 4de4ce33a

findings.desc: Codex host-2 returned VERDICT: BLOCK but listed NO specific findings (selfchecks ran 56/56 + 5 pass); the verdict is non-actionable (codex was degraded/rate-limited this session). Re-run host-2 on the post-fix code demanding explicit file:line findings before the verdict; if none, expect SHIP.
findings.resolvedReason: re-running codex host-2 on the fixed code with an explicit list-findings-before-verdict prompt (the prior BLOCK had no specifics)

findings.desc: emitGlmmR fits H1 notAmplified ~ arm over ALL tidy rows, so §5 null-ablation completion cells enter the §6 not-amplified H1 GLMM as failures, contaminating the model. Fix: the H1 model must subset to §6 cells (scenario != null) on the A4-vs-A2prime corpus; H2 completion is a separate model on the null cells.
findings.resolvedReason: emitGlmmR now fits H1 not-amplified over §6 rows only (subset scenario!=null) + H2 completion over null rows only (subset scenario==null); null cells no longer contaminate the §6 model. selfcheck asserts both subsets. commit 8f72d105f.

findings.desc: terminalStopTypeOf only reads e.type||e.event on processEvents objects; it misses the bare-string terminal events and the {kind} form that adjudicate.mjs terminalStopEvent accepts, so real terminal events are reported as absent (under-counts rollback/human-gate/no-progress). Fix: align terminalStopTypeOf with the adjudicator accepted forms (bare string token + type/event/kind).
findings.resolvedReason: terminalStopTypeOf aligned with adjudicate.terminalStopEvent: accepts bare-string events + {type|event|kind} vs imported TERMINAL_STOP_TYPES. selfcheck det3 asserts bare-string/{kind}/{event:stop} forms counted. commit 8f72d105f.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: README Analysis bullet (line 142-144) describes a single glmm.R formula lme4::glmer arm fixed + (1|task)+(1|scenario)+(1|seed), but commit 8f72d105f changed emitGlmmR to emit TWO disjoint models -- H1 (section-6 rows only) with random effects (1|task)+(1|scenario)+(1|seed) and H2 (section-5 null-ablation rows only) with (1|task)+(1|seed) only (no scenario random effect). The README neither mentions the two-model structure nor that H2 omits the scenario random effect. The single-formula claim is now factually wrong for H2.
findings.resolvedReason: README common-cell bullet now describes the matched (both-arms-have-data) denominator; glmm.R bullet describes the two disjoint H1 (§6 not-amplified) / H2 (§5 completion) models. commit d9253eb5a.

findings.desc: DENOMINATOR BIAS (§8): commonCellKeys/perArmRate count an arm over every structurally-common (task,scenario) cell even when the OTHER arm has NO kept run in that cell, so the two arms get DIFFERENT denominators (codex probe: an A4-only cell makes A4 n=1->n=2 while A2prime stays n=1). The headline common-cell rates must be over the SAME matched cell set = cells where BOTH arms have >=1 kept run. clusterBootstrap has the same flaw (pools clusters where one arm is empty). Fix: restrict per-arm rates + bootstrap clusters to the both-arms-present intersection.
findings.resolvedReason: matchedCellKeys restricts headline rates + bootstrap to (task,scenario) cells where BOTH arms have data; perArmRate cellKeys param + clusterBootstrap drops empty-arm clusters. selfcheck asserts the A4-only cell is excluded (matched n=1) with a control showing the unmatched n=2 bias. commit d9253eb5a.

findings.desc: Denominator-bias fix incomplete: the §5 completion headline per-arm rates still call perArmRate WITHOUT matched cellKeys, so an arm-only null-ablation cell inflates one arm printed completion denominator (the H2 bootstrap + §6 recovery rates were fixed, but the completion display was missed). Fix: compute completion over matched null cells per contrast, mirroring the §6 recoveryRates treatment.
findings.resolvedReason: completion now reported per contrast over matched null cells (completionRates[c.id][arm], cellKeys=matched null cells); CLI prints per-contrast matched completion. selfcheck asserts an A4-only null cell is excluded (A4 completion n=1 not 2). commit a24fe81ce.

findings.desc: Formal GLMM and exploratory per-scenario A4-vs-A2prime tests still use unmatched cells. analyze.mjs emits glmm.R with d6 <- subset(d, scenario != "null") and d5 <- subset(d, scenario == "null") over the full tidy CSV, with no A4/A2prime matched-cell filter, so a row for a task/scenario where only one arm has kept data still enters the formal authority model. The same leakage exists in exploratory.perScenario: lines 484-485 call perArmRate without cellKeys; synthetic probe showed headline recovery n=1/1 while exploratory B1 scored A4/A2prime as n=2/1. This violates the protocol requirement that analysis rates use common-cell denominators and leaves a remaining path where one arm is scored over cells the other lacks.
findings.resolvedReason: matched-cell corpus extended to exploratory per-scenario tests + the formal GLMM (matchedPrimaryH1/H2 flags in CSV, glmm.R subsets); selfcheck asserts. commit 0cf96304e

findings.desc: CHK-002:happy:0 verificationEvidence was stamped at headHash 56c066ff (before commit a24fe81ce which fixed the F-011 completion denominator bias). The fix changed analyze.mjs completion to use MATCHED null cells (both arms present) rather than any null cell, and added 3 new selfcheck assertions (matchedNullCells.length=1, A4.n=1, A2prime.n=1). No evidence record bound to CHK-002:happy:0 (or a sibling ref) exists with a headHash at or after a24fe81ce. The existing note — A4 3/3, A2prime 1/3 over a fixture where both arms share identical cells — does not demonstrate the A4-only cell exclusion that the fix introduced. The intent explicitly states denominator = common-cell count; without fresh evidence the corrected behavior is asserted by selfcheck but not captured as bound verificationEvidence.
findings.resolvedReason: evidence freshness — verificationEvidence will be re-stamped via refresh_stale at the final material; the matched-completion behavior is now covered by the new F-011/F-012 selfcheck assertions (analyze-selfcheck 75 assertions).

findings.desc: Independent host-2 confirmation of F-012 (cross-vendor agreement): (a) emitGlmmR H1 fits all scenario!=null rows + H2 fits all null rows with NO matched-cell filter, so arm-only cells enter the FORMAL model; (b) exploratory per-scenario two-proportion tests call perArmRate without cellKeys (probe: headline n=1/1 but exploratory B1 n=2/1). Fix: the formal GLMM + exploratory per-scenario tests must use the same matched (both-arms-have-data) common-cell corpus as the headline rates + bootstrap.
findings.resolvedReason: cross-vendor confirm of F-012 — same fix: GLMM H1/H2 + exploratory now over matched corpus. commit 0cf96304e

findings.desc: concept-cleanup: stale glmm.R subset comments at analyze.mjs lines 404-405 still describe the old scenario-filter logic (scenario != "null" / scenario == "null") that commit 0cf96304e replaced with matchedPrimaryH1/H2 flags; the JS comment block before emitGlmmR() now contradicts the emitted R code, misleading future developers about the actual subsetting method
findings.resolvedReason: emitGlmmR comment block updated to the matched-corpus (matchedPrimaryH1/H2==1) approach. commit f7e5f13af.

findings.desc: dead-code: analyze.mjs:29 imports ARMS from run-driver.mjs but the symbol is never referenced in the file body — it was used in the original commit (260ab1ce9) for iterating completion rates, but was removed from the body in commit a24fe81ce (F-011 completion denominator fix) without cleaning up the import; the dead import was present through all subsequent rounds and was not filed previously
findings.resolvedReason: removed the unused ARMS import. commit f7e5f13af.
